rationale:
Evidence from the development simulator (60 trials, baseline design): the oval finishes 40% of the time, with 0.75 line-loss events per run and max_error 0.055. The s-bend and slalom never finish. They end off-track with about 2 line-loss events per run, and s-bend max_error reaches 0.0635, above the 0.06 m limit. The failure mode is losing the line on bends, not running out of time. Evaluator feedback says the candidate has no race telemetry yet, so this change is based on the simulator aggregates, not a race of this candidate.

Changes and reasons:
1. Geometry: widen sensor coverage from x = ±0.024 to ±0.030 (spacing 0.015 m) and enlarge the footprint from 12 mm to 16 mm. The original array lost the line once the robot drifted about 0.03 m from centre, which matches the line-loss events. A 16 mm footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape, so the readings stay non-zero during larger offsets.
2. Controller kp from 2.5 to 3.5: the bends are where max_error exceeds the limit, so tighter proportional response should keep the robot nearer the centre line.
3. Controller kd from 0.3 to 0.6: the baseline oscillation (about 0.2 to 0.25) will probably rise with higher kp, so more derivative damping is included now rather than after a failure.
4. base_speed stays at 1.5. The oval mean finish time of 1.87 s shows that 1.5 m/s is needed to finish within 3 s, so lowering speed would likely lose completion.
5. ki, sensor_weights, line_loss, wheel geometry and mass are unchanged, so the race isolates the sensor-coverage and gain effects.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06, and better finish rate on the oval. Hypotheses to test next: (a) wider coverage reduces line-loss events; (b) kd 0.6 keeps steering_oscillation below about 0.2 with the higher kp. If line_loss_events stays high, reduce base_speed to about 1.3 and accept a slower finish. If oscillation rises above 0.3, raise kd to about 0.8.
